CLAIM DECISION LETTER
Sunridge Mutual Insurance
Claim #HC-88231 -- Approved net payout: $1,847.32

Dear Policyholder,

This letter confirms that your claim for water damage to your basement flooring has been
approved. After applying your policy's deductible and co-insurance requirement as detailed
below, your net payout is $1,847.32, which will be deposited to your account on file within 5-7
business days of this letter.

1. Your Policy Coverage
Your homeowner's policy (Policy #HP-56610) includes water-damage coverage up to a per-incident
limit of $10,000.00, subject to a $500.00 deductible per claim. Your plan also includes a 20%
co-insurance requirement specifically on water-damage claims: after the deductible is applied,
the insurer covers 80% of the remaining repair cost, and you are responsible for the other 20%.
This co-insurance requirement does not apply to fire or wind claims under your plan, which are
reimbursed at 100% of the remaining cost after the deductible.

2. How This Claim Was Calculated
The contractor's estimate for the basement flooring repair came to $2,809.15. After subtracting
your $500.00 deductible, the remaining eligible amount is $2,309.15. Applying the 20%
co-insurance requirement, the insurer covers 80% of that amount: $2,309.15 x 0.80 = $1,847.32.
This is the net payout amount confirmed at the top of this letter.

3. For Comparison: How a Fire Claim Would Differ
Because water-damage claims and fire claims are handled differently under your plan, it may help
to see a hypothetical comparison. If this had instead been a fire-damage claim with the same
$500.00 deductible, a $3,200.00 contractor estimate would result in a remaining eligible amount
of $2,700.00 after the deductible, and -- since fire claims carry no co-insurance requirement --
the full $2,700.00 would be reimbursed. This example is provided for illustration only and has
no bearing on your actual water-damage claim above.

4. Appeal Rights
If you believe this calculation is incorrect, you have 60 days from the date of this letter to
file a written appeal with our claims review department. Appeals should reference your claim
number and include any additional contractor documentation you wish to have considered. A
decision on any appeal will typically be issued within 30 days of receipt.

5. Definitions
"Deductible" means the fixed amount you are responsible for on any covered claim before
insurance coverage begins. "Co-insurance" means the percentage split of costs, after the
deductible, between you and the insurer for specific claim types as defined in your policy
schedule. "Per-incident limit" means the maximum amount the policy will pay out for damage
arising from a single covered event, regardless of the contractor's estimate.

6. Payment Method
Your net payout will be sent via direct deposit to the bank account currently on file with us.
If you would prefer a paper check instead, please contact customer service at least 2 business
days before the scheduled deposit date referenced above.

7. Questions
If you have any questions about this claim or your coverage generally, please contact our claims
department. Please have your claim number, HC-88231, ready when you call.

8. Frequently Asked Questions
"Why is there a deductible at all?" The deductible is a standard feature of your policy designed
to keep monthly premiums lower by having policyholders share in the cost of smaller claims. It
applies once per covered incident, not once per repair line item, so even if your contractor's
estimate is broken into multiple categories of work, only a single $500.00 deductible is
subtracted from the total before co-insurance is applied.

"Can the per-incident limit change my payout?" Yes, if a future claim's contractor estimate
exceeds the $10,000.00 per-incident limit for water damage, the calculation above would first
cap the eligible repair amount at $10,000.00 before subtracting the deductible and applying
co-insurance. That situation does not apply to this claim, since $2,809.15 is well under the
limit, but it is included here for your reference in case of a larger future claim.

"What if I disagree with the contractor's estimate itself, rather than the math?" A disagreement
with the estimate amount itself follows a different process than a math-based appeal: you would
need to submit a competing estimate from a licensed contractor within the same 60-day window
referenced in Section 4, and our claims team will reconcile the two estimates before
recalculating any payout.

Sincerely,
Claims Department
Sunridge Mutual Insurance
